| [LIT-1006](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1006.md) | Living without Free Will | Pereboom (2001). Defends hard incompatibilism: whether determinism is true or not, we lack the free will that basic-desert moral responsibility requires. Its four-case argument runs from an agent manipulated moment by moment by neuroscientists, through programming and upbringing, to ordinary determinism. The cases do not differ in any way that matters to responsibility, so if the manipulated agent is not responsible, neither is the determined one.
